issues.description: Inconsistent type requirement for the Farm.animals attribute across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement declares the attribute as List<Animal> (problem_statement.md, line 17), while the textual instructions in Part 3 explicitly require a Set and mention using a HashSet to prevent duplicates (problem_statement.md, line 108). The provided reference implementation declares animals as a List and initializes it with an ArrayList (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, lines 9-13). The template file currently contains a TODO and does not provide a concrete declaration (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, line 4). This mismatch leaves students unsure whether they must implement animals as a List or as a Set (and whether they must prevent duplicates), which is a substantive design decision affecting field type, constructor initialization, and getter/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix:
Unify the intended collection type across all artifacts. Two practical options:
1) If uniqueness is required (preferred given the textual instructions): update the UML in problem_statement.md to show animals: Set<Animal>, update the template and reference solution to declare 'private Set<Animal> animals;', initialize it in the no-arg constructor with 'new HashSet<>()', and update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>. Update any example code/comments accordingly.
2) If a List is intended instead: remove the HashSet/Set requirement from the textual instructions in problem_statement.md and update the UML to List<Animal>. Make the template and solution consistently use List<Animal> and clarify duplicate handling in the description.
Apply the chosen change to the template, problem statement (UML/text), and solution so students have a single, clear target to implement.
